DIARY — TAYLAN KOR, JANUARY 2029

BDS post-mortem unit.

· The wound on the left temple is superficial; there is no skull fracture and no brain haemorrhage. It is not fatal in nature.
· Cause of death: acute drug poisoning. A high level of a prescription sedative (benzodiazepine group) was found in the blood; taken together with alcohol.
· Estimated time of death: 02.10 – 02.50.
· The concentration in the blood and the metabolite level suggest the substance may have been taken about 2–4 hours before death.
· Partly digested stomach contents consistent with an evening meal.
POST-MORTEM AND TOXICOLOGY REPORT — TAYLAN KOR

There was no sedative in Baran’s glass or in Taylan’s; the substance had been taken before he came to the office.
Nehir entered the office after the time-of-death window, at 02.57; she had received the message while Taylan was alive.
The substance was taken 2–4 hours before death; at that time Taylan was sitting opposite Pelin at Kıyı Lokantası. In the record her hand is over the glass; she described it herself.
Serkan’s blow was not fatal; the death came from the drug, at least half an hour after he left.
The act that caused the death could be determined through the restaurant record and the toxicology report.

15 January 2029, 03.18. Karaköy, Sarnıç İş Hanı on Kemeraltı Caddesi, 4th floor, office 407.

The night cleaner, Gülsüm Fidan, found the self-employed accountant Taylan Kor (44) lying motionless on the floor of the office. The medical team confirmed death at the scene.

Initial findings: trauma to the head, signs of a struggle in the office, open drawers, a missing laptop, an open back window. The building’s entrance camera shows one person coming to the office during the night.

Taylan Kor’s estranged wife, Pelin Kor, has been informed.

First statement of the identified person.
I won’t discuss that without my lawyer.

Interview held after being shown the entrance camera.

Serkan Ural — second interview

…I went. I was going to ask for the money. I went up; he opened the door. He was odd, speaking slowly; I thought he was drunk. We shouted. We went for each other. I pushed him; he hit the corner of the desk. When I saw the blood I got scared and left.
His hands were trembling.
The person who entered the building at 00.47 is you.

The entrance camera pointed to Serkan, the print on the glass to Baran, the burnt SSD to Nehir; each was true, but none explained the death. The post-mortem report’s ‘2–4 hours before’ moved the time window back; the card transactions pointed to the restaurant, the old phone to the threat and the restaurant record to the glass. The building plan and the goods lift log accounted for two entries the main camera did not see.

All the evidence can be true and the story you build can still be wrong. A night is not a single event; the person who looks most suspicious, and the person found at the scene of the death, may not be the culprit.
Karaköy · Şişli · Üsküdar — 14–15 January 2029

For years Taylan Kor had been copying his clients’ sensitive financial information and selling some of it; he was also threatening his estranged wife Pelin with her father’s files. On the evening of 14 January at Kıyı Lokantası, when Taylan left the table, Pelin put her own sleeping pills in his glass. Taylan went back to his office. At 00.47 he fought with Serkan Ural, who had come over a debt; he hit the desk but stayed on his feet. At 01.07 he let Baran Tekin in by the goods lift and sold him a rival firm’s documents. Once he was alone, the drug finished its work; he died between 02.10 and 02.50. Before that, at 02.04, he had written ‘come’ to Nehir Kalkan. Nehir came at 02.57 with the guest card, found him dead, took the computer that held her own unauthorised investigation, staged the office as a burglary and, before dawn, burned it together with her car.
Who is responsible for the act that caused Taylan Kor’s death?
